title: Capacitor camera and location plugins with permissions
when: The user wants to call the phone camera or location from a Capacitor app, with permission prompts done right and a web fallback.
inputs: why the app needs them (for usage strings)
prompt: Goal: native.js wraps the camera and location plugins behind small async functions that explain, ask, handle denial and fall back on the web. Steps: 1. Add @capacitor/camera and @capacitor/geolocation, then npx cap sync. 2. native.js exports takePhoto() and whereAmI(); off native (Capacitor.isNativePlatform() false) use a file input and navigator.geolocation. 3. const s = await Camera.checkPermissions(); if s.camera is "prompt", show a short reason, then Camera.requestPermissions({ permissions: ["camera"] }). 4. On "denied", explain the system settings path and stop; never ask in a loop. 5. Photo: Camera.getPhoto({ quality: 80, width: 1600, resultType: CameraResultType.Uri, source: CameraSource.Prompt }); show photo.webPath in an . 6. Geolocation.getCurrentPosition({ timeout: 10000, maximumAge: 60000 }); on timeout offer manual entry. 7. Native usage strings: NSCameraUsageDescription and NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription in Info.plist, camera and location permissions in the other platform manifest. Quality bar: - Permission is asked at the moment of use, after a tap. Pitfalls: - Closing the camera rejects the promise; treat it as cancel, not an error. - Missing usage strings crash on first use and fail the store review. Verify: - [ ] Every plugin call sits in try/catch. - [ ] checkPermissions runs before requestPermissions. - [ ] Usage strings are listed in the README for both native projects. Output: native.js, the permission UI snippet and README notes on native permission files.

examples.input: add take photo and my location buttons to my Capacitor app
examples.output: native.js with takePhoto and whereAmI, check then request permissions, cancel handled, web fallback
